description: 'GLI3 is a 1580-residue Kruppel-type C2H2 zinc-finger transcription factor of the Ci/GLI
  family and the principal repressor-forming GLI paralog in vertebrates. Five tandem zinc fingers
  read the GLI consensus element 5''-GACCACCCA-3'' in RNA polymerase II cis-regulatory regions of
  Hedgehog target genes such as PTCH1, GLI1 and GLI2. The protein exists as two functionally opposite
  products whose ratio is set by Hedgehog signalling. In the absence of ligand, protein kinase A phosphorylates
  a cluster of sites in the C-terminal region of full-length GLI3, priming further phosphorylation
  by casein kinase 1 and glycogen synthase kinase 3; the resulting phosphodegron is recognised by
  the SCF(beta-TrCP) ubiquitin ligase and limited proteasomal proteolysis removes the C-terminal activation
  domain, yielding the roughly 83 kDa N-terminal repressor GLI3R. GLI3R enters the nucleus, occupies
  GLI sites and shuts target genes off, both through an HDAC-independent repressor domain in its N-terminal
  half and by recruiting SKI-bridged mSin3A/HDAC corepressor complexes. GLI3R is the quantitatively
  dominant form, so much of Hedgehog biology consists of relieving GLI3R repression rather than gaining
  activation. Hedgehog stimulation blocks processing: full-length GLI3 accumulates within minutes
  at the tip of the primary cilium, is released from its inhibitor SUFU, and acts in the nucleus as
  a transcriptional activator, engaging the histone acetyltransferase CBP and the MED12 interface
  of the Mediator complex through its C-terminal transactivation domain. Both forms are held in the
  cytoplasm by SUFU and DZIP1, traffic through the primary cilium in an intraflagellar-transport-
  and KIF7-dependent manner, and are further modulated by ZIC family partners, TRPS1, PP2A/mTORC1
  signalling and SPOP-CUL3-directed degradation. Through this activator/repressor switch GLI3 patterns
  the anteroposterior limb axis and the digits, the craniofacial skeleton, the forebrain and the neural
  tube, and it also regulates thymocyte development; GLI3R additionally antagonises canonical Wnt/beta-catenin
  signalling by binding the beta-catenin transactivation region. Human GLI3 mutations cause Greig
  cephalopolysyndactyly syndrome, Pallister-Hall syndrome and preaxial and postaxial polydactylies.'

    summary: Repression of RNA polymerase II target genes by the processed N-terminal form GLI3R.

- description: Sequence-specific occupancy of GLI consensus elements in RNA polymerase II cis-regulatory
    regions. The five C2H2 zinc fingers lie in the N-terminal half of the protein and are therefore
    retained by both the full-length activator and the processed repressor, which is why the same
    DNA-binding activity underlies both outputs.

    supporting_text: Furthermore, when produced in vitro, the GLI3 protein bound specifically to genomic

  - reference_id: PMID:10075717
    supporting_text: GLI3 directly binds to the Gli1 promoter and induces Gli1 transcription in response
      to Shh.
  - reference_id: Reactome:R-HSA-5612508
    supporting_text: GLI3R is a DNA-binding transcriptional repressor that recognizes consensus GLI
      sites
- description: Repression of Hedgehog target genes by the proteolytically processed N-terminal form
    GLI3R (UniProtKB:P10071-PRO_0000406137). GLI3R is generated by PKA-primed phosphorylation and
    SCF(beta-TrCP)-dependent limited proteolysis in the pathway-off state, translocates to the nucleus,
    and shuts off GLI-site target genes both through an HDAC-independent N-terminal repressor domain
    and by recruiting SKI-bridged deacetylase complexes. This is the dominant output of the gene and
    the activity assigned to GLI3R in the curated human Hedgehog GO-CAM.
  molecular_function:

- question: Should GO adopt form-specific annotation for GLI3 as a matter of routine, attaching GO:0001227
    to UniProtKB:P10071-PRO_0000406137 and GO:0001228 to UniProtKB:P10071-PRO_0000047202, as the curated

    and how much is inferred from the fact that processing requires ciliary transit? GFP-tagged Gli
    proteins were not detected at the basal body in mouse limb bud cells, yet six Reactome reactions
    and one ARBA rule place GLI3 there.

    established in mouse mutants, hold for human GLI3, and is there any thymic phenotype in Greig
    or Pallister-Hall syndrome that would justify propagating those terms to the human gene?

    restricted to the neural tube context in which it was demonstrated? This determines whether GO:0090090
    should be treated as a core GLI3 process or as the context-limited activity recorded here.

- hypothesis: The two GLI3 proteolytic products have non-overlapping genomic binding repertoires,
    not merely opposite effects at shared sites.
  description: Perform form-resolved ChIP-seq in a human cell line by tagging the endogenous locus
    with an N-terminal epitope (labelling both products) and a C-terminal epitope (labelling only
    the full-length activator), in the presence and absence of Smoothened agonist. Subtracting the
    C-terminal from the N-terminal profile gives the GLI3R-specific cistrome and would establish whether
